slides.title:
Drawn in the morning.
A **cartoon** one lesson later.
Your kid **describes** the scene
slides.body: Out loud, in their own words. Who's in it, what's happening, what it should feel like.
slides.example: For example: “A monster truck, a pink monster and a snowman on a rainbow. At night, with stars.”

slides.title: You both **check** the result
slides.body: Does it look like the drawing? Is anything missing? Your kid decides. You hold the keyboard.
slides.example: Things to look for: is everyone there? Is it the right time of day? Does it feel the way they wanted?

slides.title: Then **ask again**
slides.body: One change at a time, until it matches what they imagined. That's the skill. Not the tool.
slides.example: For example: “Make the rainbow glow. Put lights in the sky.”

slides.title:
The idea is theirs.
AI just **draws faster**.
slides.body: Try it this weekend with any drawing from the fridge.
